patient.name: Eleanor Voss
patient.chiefComplaint: Severe shortness of breath with pink frothy sputum

history.hpi: Daughter reports the patient became acutely short of breath over the last hour while resting in her recliner, with pink frothy sputum and increasing anxiety. No chest pain reported, denies fever or recent illness. Patient has a history of pulmonary arterial hypertension managed with sildenafil.
medications: Sildenafil 20 mg PO three times daily (for pulmonary hypertension)
history.lastOralIntake: Dinner approximately 3 hours prior to onset
history.events: Daughter called 911 after finding the patient acutely dyspneic, unable to speak in full sentences

scene.location: Single-story home, patient found tripoding in a recliner in the living room
scene.bystanders: Daughter present, provides medication list and timeline
visualCues: Patient tripoding in recliner, using accessory muscles
Pink frothy sputum at the corners of the mouth
Bilateral pitting edema to the shins
Home oxygen concentrator present in the corner, not in use

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 76-year-old female in severe respiratory distress, tripoding, with pink frothy sputum, JVD, and diffuse bilateral rales. She is hypertensive and tachypneic, speaking only single words.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, but only able to speak single words
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Severe accessory muscle use, diffuse bilateral rales to the apices, pink frothy sputum at the lips
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses bounding, skin pale and diaphoretic
otherFindings: Bilateral 2+ pitting edema to the shins
Unable to lie flat, insists on sitting upright

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply CPAP with PEEP 5 cmH2O, coach patient, titrate for air hunger and SpO2 ≥94%
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Restoration of adequate oxygenation and ventilation should precede or be accomplished simultaneously with other medication therapies below. CPAP/BiPAP: See Airway Management Guideline for goals of care and escalation of interventions
expectedActions.rationale: Non-invasive ventilation is first-line for hypertensive pulmonary edema and improves oxygenation before or alongside nitrate therapy.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Screen medication list for PDE5 inhibitor or IV pulmonary-hypertension therapy before giving nitroglycerin
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The use of nitrates should be avoided in any patient who has used a phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours. Examples are sildenafil, vardenafil and tadalafil, which are used for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension. Also avoid use in patients receiving intravenous epoprostenol or treporstenil which are used for pulmonary hypertension
expectedActions.rationale: Sildenafil combined with nitrates causes profound, refractory vasodilatory hypotension.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL for SBP ≥160 mmHg; may repeat every 5 min while SBP >100
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP >= 160 mmHg or MAP greater than 120: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL, can repeat every 5 minutes for SBP greater than 100 mmHg. Consider IV nitroglycerin infusion titrated to blood pressure
expectedActions.rationale: High-dose nitrates reduce preload and afterload rapidly in hypertensive pulmonary edema once the PDE5-inhibitor screen is clear.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.if: CPAP applied and med list screened
transitions.condition: Crew recognizes severe hypertensive pulmonary edema, applies CPAP with PEEP, and screens the medication list for nitrate contraindications before starting high-dose nitroglycerin.

Crew administers high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin without asking about PDE5-inhibitor or IV pulmonary-hypertension therapy use; the patient's home sildenafil, taken that afternoon, potentiates the nitrate's vasodilatory effect.

phases.name: CPAP applied and med list screened
phases.description: Crew applies CPAP with PEEP, obtains a full medication history including the patient's sildenafil use for pulmonary hypertension, and titrates high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin per the severe-hypertension dosing tier.
phases.triggerCondition: After the primary assessment confirms severe pulmonary edema with SBP 224/118, the crew initiates CPAP and specifically screens for phosphodiesterase-inhibitor or IV pulmonary-hypertension therapy use before starting high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, CPAP mask in place with good seal
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Accessory muscle use decreasing, air movement improved on CPAP
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses bounding, skin still diaphoretic
otherFindings: CPAP mask sealed, tolerating well after coaching
Daughter confirms sildenafil 20 mg three times daily for pulmonary hypertension

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain continuous CPAP mask seal through transport; do not break seal until ED handoff
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Once initiated and patient is tolerating mask, DO NOT discontinue CPAP/BiPAP until patient is on the emergency department stretcher and hospital CPAP/BiPAP is immediately available for patient to be switched over, or physician is at bedside and requesting CPAP/BiPAP be discontinued. Breaking the mask seal causes a significant decrease in airway pressures and may lead to abrupt decompensation due to atelectasis and alveolar collapse.
expectedActions.rationale: Breaking the CPAP seal en route risks rapid decompensation back into overt pulmonary edema.

expectedActions.shortAction: Continuously monitor pulse oximetry and waveform capnography to guide ongoing therapy
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patients with significant respiratory distress should have continuous pulse oximetry and waveform capnography monitoring for both assessment and for guiding therapy
expectedActions.rationale: Serial monitoring confirms the nitrate/CPAP combination is working and flags early deterioration.

transitions.condition: Medication screen confirms no recent PDE5-inhibitor or IV pulmonary-hypertension therapy use; nitroglycerin and CPAP are continued with improving vitals.

phases.name: Med screen clear, nitro tolerated
phases.description: With the medication screen clear, CPAP and titrated nitroglycerin steadily improve oxygenation and reduce blood pressure without the vasodilatory crash risked by a nitrate-PDE5i interaction. Mask seal is maintained continuously through transport.
phases.triggerCondition: After the med screen confirms no PDE5-inhibitor use, nitroglycerin is repeated per the SBP tier and CPAP is maintained without interruption; oxygenation and blood pressure trend toward goal.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Minimal accessory muscle use, air entry improved bilaterally
otherFindings: CPAP mask seal maintained without interruption

phases.name: Nitro given without med screen
phases.description: Nitroglycerin was given without screening for PDE5-inhibitor use. The patient's home sildenafil potentiates the nitrate's vasodilatory effect, producing profound, refractory hypotension superimposed on her pulmonary edema.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew administers repeated high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin without asking about PDE5-inhibitor or IV pulmonary-hypertension therapy use; the sildenafil-nitrate interaction produces a sudden, severe drop in blood pressure.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, CPAP mask still in place
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and thready, skin pale and cool
otherFindings: Sudden onset of dizziness and diaphoresis after third nitroglycerin dose
Rales persist despite falling blood pressure
Daughter now recalls the sildenafil use when directly asked again

expectedActions.shortAction: 500 mL NS pressure-infused bolus for nitrate-induced hypotension; stop if pulmonary edema worsens
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: IV fluid volume goal attained by giving boluses that are pressure infused over less than 15 minutes each based on patient's condition and clinical impression. Fluid goal of up to 30 mL/kg of isotonic fluid by administering rapid, predetermined boluses (e.g., 500 mL) unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops
expectedActions.rationale: A cautious fluid bolus addresses the vasodilatory hypotension while watching closely for worsening pulmonary edema.

expectedActions.shortAction: Norepinephrine infusion 3.4 mcg/min IV (68 kg × 0.05 mcg/kg/min), titrate up to 34 mcg/min to MAP ≥65 if hypotension persists
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Vasopressors (shock unresponsive to IV fluids) titrated to physiologic targets. Cardiogenic, hypovolemic, obstructive shock and distributive shock: Norepinephrine 0.05–0.5 mcg/kg/minute
expectedActions.rationale: Refractory nitrate-induced hypotension unresponsive to a cautious fluid bolus requires a vasopressor to restore perfusion.
